- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.15) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.15), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% if recent price is trending up.  
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days) are common; cap forecast at 10% above peak for next 3–5 days.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecast days are above 10% above recent 18-day average, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags by 1–3 days; if sentiment is volatile, add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment weight to forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated +0.10 to +0.20 spikes, model tends to overreact; dampen forecast by 3–7% for next 5 days.
